A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAC-Opt research. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original SAC-Opt experiments, baseline reruns, ablations, cross-model evaluations, timing measurements, and an extraction-error audit. Some separately marked baseline results are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports accuracy standard deviations and a statistical analysis of verifier performance.

M1.justification: The extraction, hybrid code generation, reconstruction, verification, targeted correction, and solver-debugging procedure remains unchanged, including Algorithm 1 and the appendix prompts. Clarifications about agent nondeterminism and alternative verifiers do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven cleaned datasets: NL4OPT, IndustryOR, EasyLP, ComplexLP, NLP4LP, ReSocratic, and ComplexOR. The cutting-stock and flowshop-scheduling cases are retained; the new statistical analyses introduce no additional task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 7 retain Standard, CoT, CoE, CAFA, Reflexion, OptiMUS-0.2, and OptiMUS-0.3. New Table 8 reports uncertainty for existing comparisons. Table 5 changes unnamed best-baseline values without identifying a comparator change.

E3.justification: The shared extraction pipeline, backbones, accuracy criterion, dataset sizes, three debugging attempts, five correction iterations, and similarity threshold of 0.75 remain unchanged. The added analyses use existing results and the previously stated evaluation setting.

E4.justification: Section 4.7 adds an analysis of agreement between the two verifiers' dataset-level accuracies, and Appendix A.9 adds an accuracy-stability analysis across runs. Existing ablations, case studies, extraction audits, and correction/debugging analyses remain intact.

E5.justification: New Table 8 supplies accuracy standard deviations for SAC-Opt, Reflexion, and both OptiMUS versions across seven datasets. Section 4.7 adds Pearson correlation, R-squared, and Spearman correlation. Both versions already specify five independent runs; v3 does not establish an increase in runs or add significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds verifier correlations of 0.962 Pearson and 0.929 Spearman, R-squared of 0.925, a 6.94-point mean accuracy gap, and Table 8's standard deviations. Table 5 changes IndustryOR SAC-Opt accuracy from 63.8% to 63.7% and runtime from 80.20 to 79.00 seconds; its best-baseline accuracies change from 54.3% to 54.0% for IndustryOR and 57.1% to 52.2% for ComplexOR. These conflict with unchanged Tables 1 and 7, rather than establishing performance improvements. An introduction sentence also changes 7.8% to 7.7%.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and the mathematical definitions remain substantively unchanged. Appendix A.4 still presents an empirical convergence example, with no added theorem, proof, or formal convergence guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims of training-free, proactive semantic verification and targeted backward correction, including the headline average improvement of 7.7% and ComplexLP improvement of 21.9%.

C2.justification: v3 softens the rendering-correctness guarantee in Section 3.3, explicitly states that neither verifier is a perfect oracle, and distinguishes dataset-level correlation from human-calibrated anchor validation. Appendix A.9 adds an interpretation that the results demonstrate stability across seeds and robustness to randomness.

D1.justification: The structured-data example, parameter values, reconstruction and verification prompts, implementation settings, and source-code access information are retained. Table 8 reiterates previously disclosed settings rather than adding new implementation instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds Tsouros et al.'s Holy Grail 2.0 when discussing human feedback, plus Chandrasekaran and Mago's semantic-similarity survey and Strang's linear-algebra reference. Most other citation changes update bibliographic information while preserving the cited work's role and the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized methodological clarifications, wording corrections, and author/header edits, while most prose and section ordering remain stable. Acknowledgements and an Impact Statement are added; the former Appendix A.9 LLM-usage disclosure is removed and A.9 becomes the statistical-analysis section.

P2.justification: v3 converts the single-column preprint's main text and references to a two-column conference layout, extensively resizing and relocating retained tables, figures, the algorithm, and the case-study box. Figures 1–3 retain their underlying content, Figure 1 gains a clearer caption, and Table 8 is added.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through accuracy standard deviations and clearer qualifications about verifier reliability. However, Table 5 introduces contradictions with unchanged Tables 1 and 7, and Appendix A.9 overstates comparative stability: SAC-Opt's ComplexOR standard deviation is 5.7, versus 4.4 for Reflexion and 4.2 for OptiMUS-0.2. These reporting gains coexist with new numerical inconsistencies and unsupported interpretation, preventing a reliable net judgment of overall quality improvement.
